nodes.name: Fact 2.1: KW frontier
nodes.statement:
There is an algorithm $\mathcal A$ that achieves generation in the limit with partial
enumeration with the following guarantee: ``for any adversarial enumeration $E$ of an infinite
subset $C$ of one of the languages $K \in \mathcal X$ such that $C$ has lower density at least
$\alpha > 0$ in $K$, the set of output strings $O(E, \mathcal A)$ $[\dots]$ has a lower
density in $K$ that is at least $\alpha/2$.'' Moreover, ``$\alpha/2$ also serves as an upper
bound on the lower density achievable by any algorithm.'' In our notation: for every countable
collection $\mathcal X$ there is an element-based generator with $\underline{d}(O,H) \ge
\tfrac12\,\underline{d}(C,H)$ on every legal instance, and from some round $t^*$ on it outputs
only elements of $H$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.7: $G^*$
nodes.statement:
With the partial model and limit-set coverage:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item \textup{(Universal sweep)} The generator $G_{\mathrm{sw}}$ of (3.3) is
    sound (zero hallucination, unconditionally) and on every legal instance achieves $O
    \supseteq H \setminus C$, hence coverage $c \ge 1 - \overline{d}(C,H)$ ($\ge 1 -
    \alpha$ when $d(C,H) = \alpha$ exists), with trivia rounds among $[1\dots N]$
    bounded by $T_0 + \lfloor \sqrt N \rfloor$ ($T_0$ finite, instance-dependent): the trivia
    rate tends to $0$ while the count is infinite in general (necessarily, by
    3.6(c)).
  \item \textup{(Tight generator on $\mathcal{H}_{\alpha}$)} On the tight family $\mathcal{H}_{\alpha}$ the single
    deterministic generator $G^*$ of (3.4) achieves, with zero hallucination:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
  \item truth $K$ (any $C \subseteq K$, any order): $c \ge \max(1/2,\ 1 -
    \overline{d}(C,K))$, trivia rate $\le \lfloor \sqrt N \rfloor / N$;
  \item truth $K'$ with $C \subseteq K$ (covering all of 3.6(a)'s tight
    instances): $c \ge 1 - \alpha/2 - o(1)$, with zero trivia;
  \item truth $K'$ with $C \not\subseteq K$: $c \ge \max(1/2,\ 1 - \overline{d}(C,K'))$,
    zero trivia.
    \end{enumerate}
  \item \textup{(Finite-trivia side; restated)} 2.1 gives a generator with
    $\underline{d}(O,H) \ge \tfrac12 \underline{d}(C,H)$ for every countable collection and
    eventually zero trivia; on $\mathcal{H}_{\alpha}$ it attains $\alpha/2$ at truth $K'$ and $1/2$ at truth
    $K$, matching 3.6's caps.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Fact 2.7
nodes.statement:
A countable collection $\mathcal{H}$ admits a set-valued
generator achieving exact breadth in the limit if and only if $\mathcal{H}$ satisfies Angluin's
condition (Theorem~3.3), and admits approximate breadth in the limit if and only if $\mathcal{H}$
satisfies the weak Angluin condition (Theorem~3.8).

nodes.name: Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P} = \{(F_i, H_i)\}$ be a countable pair model (2.3), with a
relativized generator (2.4) that queries the perfect verifier $\mathbf
1_{F}$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
  \item Exact breadth in the limit on $\mathcal{P}$ is achievable if and only if every fiber
    $\mathcal{P}_{F}$ satisfies Angluin's condition.
  \item Approximate breadth in the limit on $\mathcal{P}$ is achievable if and only if every fiber
    satisfies the weak Angluin condition.
  \item In the single-ambient case $F_i \equiv F$, the relativized characterization
    coincides with the oracle-free characterization of 2.7. In the multi-ambient
    case the verifier's entire information content, for the in-the-limit breadth goal, is
    exactly ambient identification: locating which $F$ is realized, after which it adds
    nothing.
  \item \textup{(Zero-discrimination.)} For $H_i, H_j$ in the same fiber the oracle is
    the identical function $\mathbf 1_{F}$; the realized query path and output at any
    prefix $S_n$ are identical across the two instances. Every behavioral distinction
    within a fiber is driven by the enumeration alone.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Lemma D.2
nodes.statement:
Work over $U = \mathbb{N} \times \{0,1\}$. Let $L^* = U_0$ (column $0$), let the spine be the
even column-$0$ indices $R = \{(2m, 0) : m \ge 0\}$, and set $H_j = L^* \setminus R_{\ge
j}$ with $R_{\ge j} = \{(2m, 0) : m \ge j\}$. Let $F_j = H_j \cup A_j$ and $F_\infty
= L^* \cup A_\infty$ with $A_j, A_\infty \subseteq U_1$ (column $1$) infinite. Then for
every $j$, every finite $S \subseteq U$, and every $G \subseteq U$, $G$ cannot
satisfy both
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item $L^* \setminus S \subseteq G \subseteq F_\infty$,
  \item $H_j \setminus S \subseteq G \subseteq F_j$.
\end{enumerate}
nodes.section: Figure 7: Dependency map. Dashed boxes are restated prior facts; solid boxes are results o

nodes.name: Lemma D.3
nodes.statement:
With the parameters of D.2: for every finite $T \subseteq L^*$ and every $N
\in \mathbb{N}$ there is $j \ge N$ with $T \subseteq H_j \subsetneq L^*$ and $L^* \setminus H_j
= R_{\ge j}$ infinite. Consequently $\{H_j\}_j \cup \{L^*\}$ is a Gold-style ascending
chain with union $L^*$, non-identifiable from positive data, and $L^*$ violates Angluin's
condition in this collection.
nodes.section: Figure 7: Dependency map. Dashed boxes are restated prior facts; solid boxes are results o

nodes.name: Theorem 3.2
nodes.statement:
In the pair model with the protocol of 2.3:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
  \item \textup{(Exhaustive generator)} With the verifier $\mathbf 1_{F}$, the generator
    $G_n = F \setminus S_n$ achieves sound coverage in the limit on every countable
    pair model: at every round, it has zero hallucination, and (when $F \setminus H$ is
    infinite) infinitely many trivia.
  \item \textup{(Separation)} There is a countable pair model $\mathcal{P}^{\dagger}$ (all
    languages infinite, every $F_i \setminus H_i$ infinite) on which no oracle-free
    set-valued generator (an arbitrary function of the prefix) achieves sound coverage in the
    limit.
  \item The verifier strictly enlarges the class of pair models admitting sound coverage, from
    a proper subclass to all of them; this is in contrast to breadth, where within a fiber it
    adds nothing \textup{(3.1(c))}.
\end{enumerate}
nodes.section: Figure 7: Dependency map. Dashed boxes are restated prior facts; solid boxes are results o

nodes.name: Lemma D.4
nodes.statement:
Let $K \subseteq K'$ be infinite with $d(K,K') = \alpha > 0$ exact. For any $A \subseteq
K$,
\begin{equation*}
  \overline{d}(A,K') = \alpha \cdot \overline{d}(A,K),
  \qquad
  \underline{d}(A,K') = \alpha \cdot \underline{d}(A,K).
\end{equation*}
nodes.section: Figure 7: Dependency map. Dashed boxes are restated prior facts; solid boxes are results o

nodes.name: Lemma 3.5
nodes.statement:
Let $K \subseteq U$ be infinite and let $T_{\mathrm{race}} \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ have density
$1$, with $$w(t) \coloneqq t - \left\lvert T_{\mathrm{race}} \cap [1\dots t] \right\rvert = o(t).$$
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)}]
  \item \textup{(Greedy cover)} If at every $t \in T_{\mathrm{race}}$ the generator outputs
    the $\prec$-least element of $K \setminus (S_t \cup O_{t-1})$, then against every
    adversary enumeration, $\left\lvert O \cap K[1\!\dots\! M] \right\rvert \ge \tfrac12\,(M - w(\tau_M) - 1)$ for
    all $M$, where $\tau_M$ is the index of the $M$-th race round; hence $\underline{d}(O \cap
    K,K) \ge 1/2$.
  \item \textup{(Racing cap)} The racing adversary $A_K$ of 3.4 is a legal
    repetition-free enumeration of $K$. Against it, every generator satisfies $\left\lvert O \cap
    K[1\!\dots\! M] \right\rvert \le M/2 + \log_2 M + 3$ for $M \ge 2$; hence $\overline{d}(O \cap K,K) \le 1/2$.
\end{enumerate}
nodes.section: Figure 7: Dependency map. Dashed boxes are restated prior facts; solid boxes are results o

nodes.name: Theorem 3.6
nodes.statement:
On the tight family $\mathcal{H}_{\alpha}$ of (3.1), with deterministic element-based generators
and limit-set coverage:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
  \item \textup{(Race cap)} For every deterministic generator there are two legal instances of
    $\mathcal{H}_{\alpha}$ sharing one transcript (the adversary is $A_K$ inside $K$), with coverage at most
    $1/2$ at truth $K$ and at most $1 - \alpha/2$ at truth $K'$ (revealed core $C = K$,
    density $\alpha$). Hence no generator guarantees coverage exceeding $1 - \alpha/2$ on
    $\mathcal{H}_{\alpha}$, nor exceeding $1/2$ at truth $K$.
  \item \textup{(Finite-trivia cap)} Every deterministic generator that emits finitely many
    trivia on every legal instance has coverage at most $\alpha/2$ on the truth-$K'$ racing
    instance.
  \item \textup{(Necessity of trivia)} Any generator guaranteeing coverage exceeding
    $\alpha/2$ on all of $\mathcal{H}_{\alpha}$ emits infinitely many trivia on some instance; with
    3.7\textup{(iii)}, $\alpha/2$ is exactly the finite-trivia frontier.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Fact 2.1, Fact 2.2
nodes.statement:
There is an algorithm $\mathcal A$ that achieves generation in the limit with partial
enumeration with the following guarantee: ``for any adversarial enumeration $E$ of an infinite
subset $C$ of one of the languages $K \in \mathcal X$ such that $C$ has lower density at least
$\alpha > 0$ in $K$, the set of output strings $O(E, \mathcal A)$ $[\dots]$ has a lower
density in $K$ that is at least $\alpha/2$.'' Moreover, ``$\alpha/2$ also serves as an upper
bound on the lower density achievable by any algorithm.'' In our notation: for every countable
collection $\mathcal X$ there is an element-based generator with $\underline{d}(O,H) \ge
\tfrac12\,\underline{d}(C,H)$ on every legal instance, and from some round $t^*$ on it outputs
only elements of $H$.

For the identified-intersection sequence $\mathcal I^{(t)}$ that KW's generator maintains,
``there is a finite time $T$ such that after which all the identified intersection $\mathcal
I^{(t)}$ are valid,'' where valid means $\mathcal I^{(t)} \subset K$. The statement and its
proof are in the partial-enumeration model. In our notation: there is a finite round $T_0$
with $\mathcal I^{(t)} \subseteq H$ for all $t \ge T_0$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.7
nodes.statement:
With the partial model and limit-set coverage:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item \textup{(Universal sweep)} The generator $G_{\mathrm{sw}}$ of (3.3) is
    sound (zero hallucination, unconditionally) and on every legal instance achieves $O
    \supseteq H \setminus C$, hence coverage $c \ge 1 - \overline{d}(C,H)$ ($\ge 1 -
    \alpha$ when $d(C,H) = \alpha$ exists), with trivia rounds among $[1\dots N]$
    bounded by $T_0 + \lfloor \sqrt N \rfloor$ ($T_0$ finite, instance-dependent): the trivia
    rate tends to $0$ while the count is infinite in general (necessarily, by
    3.6(c)).
  \item \textup{(Tight generator on $\mathcal{H}_{\alpha}$)} On the tight family $\mathcal{H}_{\alpha}$ the single
    deterministic generator $G^*$ of (3.4) achieves, with zero hallucination:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
  \item truth $K$ (any $C \subseteq K$, any order): $c \ge \max(1/2,\ 1 -
    \overline{d}(C,K))$, trivia rate $\le \lfloor \sqrt N \rfloor / N$;
  \item truth $K'$ with $C \subseteq K$ (covering all of 3.6(a)'s tight
    instances): $c \ge 1 - \alpha/2 - o(1)$, with zero trivia;
  \item truth $K'$ with $C \not\subseteq K$: $c \ge \max(1/2,\ 1 - \overline{d}(C,K'))$,
    zero trivia.
    \end{enumerate}
  \item \textup{(Finite-trivia side; restated)} 2.1 gives a generator with
    $\underline{d}(O,H) \ge \tfrac12 \underline{d}(C,H)$ for every countable collection and
    eventually zero trivia; on $\mathcal{H}_{\alpha}$ it attains $\alpha/2$ at truth $K'$ and $1/2$ at truth
    $K$, matching 3.6's caps.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Remark 3.11
nodes.statement:
The proofs of 3.5, 3.6 use \emph{only} the following properties of the triple
$(K, K', F)$: a countable ground set with a canonical order; nesting $K \subsetneq K'
\subseteq F$ with all three infinite; $F \setminus K'$ infinite; and $m_N \coloneqq \left\lvert K
\cap K'[1\!\dots\! N] \right\rvert = \alpha N + O(1)$ with $\alpha > 0$ exact. Any triple meeting this
interface inherits 3.5, 3.6 verbatim. We invoke this in 4.2 to
transport the dichotomy into the compression model.

nodes.name: Proposition 4.2
nodes.statement:
In $F_n$ ($n \ge 2$), with letters $\{a, x\}$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item \textup{(Name-cut pairs at every rational $\alpha$)} The pair (4.1)
    satisfies $\left\lvert K \cap K'[1\!\dots\! N] \right\rvert = \alpha N + O(q)$, so $d(K,K') = \alpha$
    exactly; it meets the interface of 3.11, and the dichotomy
    (3.10) holds verbatim inside the compression model.
  \item \textup{(Obstruction: the bounded cut is forced)} For the unbounded cut
    $\theta_\kappa$ with dictionary-only wrapped length and nested tag-dictionaries
    ($\hat\mu_{m,i} = a a\, x^i a\, x^{q+1-i} a\, x^{2^m}$, tags $\le p$ versus all), the
    analogous pair $(\hat K, \hat K')$ has $\overline{d}(\hat K,\hat K') = 0$ (unique parsing via
    $aa$-blocks; the total count of compressible strings is exponential in $L$, the $k$-block
    counting $N_k(L) \le q^k (\log_2 L + 1)^k$ bounds the small-$k$ mass, and the tag
    restriction truncates the rest; the good-word fraction vanishes at rate $\Theta(1/\log L)$
    along prefix scales). Nested tag-pairs under unbounded cuts realize no $\alpha \in (0,1)$.
  \item \textup{(Extreme separation point)} For that pair $(\hat K, \hat K')$, finite-trivia
    sound generators have coverage $0$ at truth $\hat K'$ (same-transcript transfer and
    $\overline{d}(\hat K,\hat K') = 0$), while $G_{\mathrm{sw}}$ of 3.7(i) achieves
    coverage $1$ with vanishing trivia rate. The free regime exhibits the maximal gap of the
    dichotomy: coverage $0$ versus $1$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Proposition 4.3
nodes.statement:
In $A_n$ with base $c \ge 4$ and $\kappa < n(1 - 1/\log_2 c)$, the compressible sublanguage $H
= H_{D_c}$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
  c_1\, r^{\,1/\log_2 c - n} \ \le\ \frac{\left\lvert H \cap B_G(r) \right\rvert}{\left\lvert B_G(r) \right\rvert}
  \ \le\ c_2\, r^{-\delta}, \qquad \delta = n - \kappa - n/\log_2 c > 0,
\end{equation}
where $B_G(r)$ is the wrapped-length ball of radius $r$. The fraction of compressible
statements is polynomially small in the radius $r$, equivalently exponentially small in ABFM's
compressed scale $s$ (since $r = c^{\Theta(s)}$; interpretation only). The exhaustive
generator's precision thus tends to $0$ polynomially in volume, while the sweep generator's
precision tends to $1$.
